locations/new-york.title: New York SEO company: how we rank NYC businesses
locations/new-york.intro: New York is the most competitive local search market in the country. This is how RankEmpire works as a search engine optimization company for New York City businesses, what our NYC SEO services include, and what to expect from any New York SEO agency you hire.

sections.h: What a New York SEO company should do first
sections.p: Start with the borough and neighborhood map, not a keyword list. A Brooklyn contractor, a Manhattan law firm and a Queens restaurant compete in different results, so we map which neighborhoods produce your customers, check where you appear from each of them on a rank grid, and build the plan around the gaps. Then come the technical audit, the Google Business Profile and the service pages, in that order, as described in our [90-day local SEO roadmap](/blog/local-seo-90-day-roadmap/).

sections.h: SEO services for New York businesses
sections.p: Our New York programs combine [local SEO](/local-seo/) for the map pack, [Google Business Profile optimization](/google-business-profile-seo/), neighborhood and service pages written for each borough, [technical SEO](/technical-seo/) and [link building](/link-building/) from New York publications, associations and partners. Every plan also covers answer engines and AI assistants, because New Yorkers increasingly ask ChatGPT or Google AI Mode for recommendations instead of scrolling results. We run these programs for the industries that compete hardest in the city, including [law firms](/seo-for-lawyers/), [dentists](/seo-for-dentists/), [restaurants](/seo-for-restaurants/) and [electricians](/seo-for-electricians/).

sections.h: How much SEO costs in New York
sections.p: NYC SEO usually costs more than the national average because competition is denser and rankings take more content and authority to win. Single-location local plans start at $599 a month with RankEmpire; businesses competing across several boroughs or citywide typically need the Pro or Multi-location plan. Our [SEO cost guide](/blog/how-much-does-seo-cost/) explains the ranges and what drives them, and every plan is month to month after onboarding.

sections.h: How long SEO takes in NYC
sections.p: Expect movement on neighborhood and long-tail searches within 60 to 90 days, and on competitive citywide terms like seo company nyc after four to six months or more, depending on your starting authority. The first visible sign is usually impressions in Search Console, then average position, then calls and form leads.

seo-tools/backlink-checker.title: How to use a free backlink checker to check backlinks and find link opportunities
seo-tools/backlink-checker.intro: A backlink checker shows which websites link to yours, which pages they point to and what anchor text they use. Backlinks are still one of the strongest ranking signals in Google, and they increasingly shape which brands AI assistants trust and cite. This free SEO backlink checker tool analyzes a link export privately in your browser, so you can check backlinks without signing up or sharing your data.

sections.h: How to check backlinks for free
sections.p: Export your links from Google Search Console (Links, then Top linking sites or Top linked pages, then Export), or from Bing Webmaster Tools, Ahrefs Webmaster Tools or any SEO tool you already use. Paste the export into the backlink checker above with your domain, and it groups the links by referring domain, flags the anchor text mix and highlights the pages that attract the most links. Search Console is the most reliable free source because it comes straight from Google.

sections.h: What to look for in a backlink search
sections.p: Look for the number of distinct referring domains rather than total links, the share of links pointing to your money pages versus the homepage, a natural anchor text mix (mostly brand and URL anchors, few exact-match keywords), and links from sites relevant to your industry or city. A handful of relevant local or industry links is worth more than hundreds of directory links.

sections.h: How to spot toxic or spammy backlinks
sections.p: Warning signs include sudden spikes of links from unrelated foreign sites, links from obvious link farms or private blog networks, sitewide footer links with keyword anchors, and pages that exist only to link out. Google ignores most of these automatically, so disavowing is rarely needed; reserve it for a manual action or a known paid-link history.

sections.h: Turning backlink data into new links
sections.p: Use the backlink checker on two or three competitors as well as your own site. The sites linking to them but not to you are your best outreach list: industry associations, local news, suppliers, directories and publications that already link to businesses like yours. Our [link building](/link-building/) and [off-page SEO](/off-page-seo/) services do this outreach for you, and a [competitor SEO analysis](/competitor-seo-analysis/) maps the full gap.

sections.h: Free backlink checker vs paid SEO tools
sections.p: Free backlink checker tools online are ideal for a quick audit of your own profile using Search Console data. Paid tools add their own web crawl, historic link data and metrics for any domain, which helps for large-scale outreach. For most local and small businesses, Search Console plus this tool covers what matters. Pair it with our other [free SEO tools](/seo-tools/), such as the [website SEO checker](/seo-tools/website-seo-checker/).

sections.p: A Google Business Profile for the showroom with photos, products and hours; a page for each material and service (hardwood installation, LVP, tile, carpet, refinishing, commercial flooring); project galleries by neighborhood; review requests after installs; and Product and Service schema so search engines understand your range.

sections.h: Flooring company SEO marketing for research searches
sections.p: Searches like LVP vs hardwood, how much does hardwood flooring cost per square foot and best flooring for pets are researched long before a purchase. Guides that answer them honestly, with price ranges and installation details, earn rankings, links from home improvement sites and citations in AI answers, and send buyers to your showroom pages.

sections.h: Google Business Profile management for flooring stores
sections.p: The showroom profile is where most local flooring searches end. List every product line and service, post new arrivals and completed projects weekly, and keep hours and appointment links accurate. Our [Google Business Profile checklist](/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/) covers every item.

sections.h: Choosing the best flooring SEO company

sections.h: Medical practice search engine optimization and E-E-A-T
sections.p: Health pages rank when they show expertise and trust: named physician authors, credentials, review dates, citations to medical sources and clear practice information. Thin or unreviewed medical content rarely ranks and can drag down the rest of the site.

sections.h: Local SEO for physicians and clinics

Each office needs its own profile, page and reviews, and each provider should be listed accurately on the platforms patients and AI assistants check. See our [local SEO](/local-seo/) approach and the [Google Business Profile checklist](/blog/google-business-profile-optimization-checklist/).

sections.h: National SEO vs local SEO
sections.p: Local SEO wins searches near a location through the map pack and local signals. National SEO wins searches anywhere through authority and content. Many brands need both: national pages for category terms and [local SEO](/local-seo/) for each location or service area.

sections.h: Choosing a national SEO company

aeo.title: Answer engine optimization: how to win featured snippets and AI answers
aeo.intro: Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the practice of structuring pages so search engines, voice assistants and AI answer boxes can lift a direct answer from them. It focuses on the passage rather than the page: a real question as the heading, a complete answer in the first two sentences, and schema that labels what each block is.

sections.h: What answer engine optimization includes
sections.p: Question research from Search Console and People Also Ask, rewritten headings and openings that answer first, FAQ blocks where the questions are unique to the page, FAQPage, HowTo, Service and Organization schema, Speakable markup for voice assistants, and monthly tracking of the featured snippets, People Also Ask results and AI Overview citations you own.

sections.h: Featured snippets on Google
sections.p: Google pulls featured snippets from pages that already rank on page one and answer the query in a short, self-contained passage: a 40 to 60 word definition, a numbered list for steps, or a table for comparisons. Formatting the right passage under the right heading is often enough to take a snippet from a competitor.

sections.h: AEO vs SEO vs GEO
sections.p: SEO gets a page ranked, AEO gets its best passage quoted, and [generative engine optimization](/geo/) gets the brand cited inside AI answers. Most of the work overlaps, which is why we run them as one program; the full comparison is in our guide to [AEO vs GEO vs SEO](/blog/aeo-vs-geo-vs-seo/), and the next step, AI agents, is covered in [AI agent optimization](/blog/ai-agent-optimization/).

sections.h: How to measure AEO
sections.p: Track the featured snippets and People Also Ask results you own, impressions on queries where you have no clicks (often a sign you are the zero-click answer), and citations in AI Overviews for a fixed set of questions. Our monthly reports show these next to rankings and leads.

international-seo.title: International SEO: how to rank in new countries and languages
international-seo.intro: International SEO makes a website rank correctly for each country and language it targets. It decides which version of a page Google shows to a searcher in Germany, Mexico or Canada, and it fails quietly: a brand can publish translated pages and still show the wrong country version, split its authority, or not rank abroad at all.

sections.h: Choosing a structure: ccTLDs, subdomains or subfolders
sections.p: Country domains (example.de) send the strongest local signal but split authority across sites and cost more to run. Subdomains (de.example.com) are easier to host separately but are treated partly as separate sites. Subfolders (example.com/de/) keep all authority on one domain and are the right default for most US brands expanding abroad. The choice should follow your legal, hosting and team setup, not habit.

sections.h: Hreflang done right
sections.p: Hreflang tags tell Google which language and country each URL serves and which pages are equivalents. Every version must reference every other version and itself, use valid language and region codes, and point to indexable, canonical URLs. Missing return links and hreflang pointing to redirected or noindexed pages are the most common errors; our [technical SEO](/technical-seo/) audits check every pair.

sections.h: Localization, not just translation
sections.p: Searchers in each market use different words, currencies, units and examples. Keyword research per country, local pricing and shipping details, and native-speaker review turn a translated page into one that ranks and converts. Machine translation without review rarely ranks.

sections.h: Earning authority in each market
sections.p: Links and mentions from sites in the target country carry the most weight there. Local press, industry associations, partners and directories in each market build that authority, alongside [link building](/link-building/) for the main domain.

sections.h: International SEO for US brands and for brands entering the US
sections.p: We support US companies expanding abroad and international brands entering the US market. For large multi-country sites, see [enterprise SEO](/enterprise-seo/); for companies selling across the US only, [national SEO](/national-seo/) is the better fit.
